label: Broken Expectation
line: Open on a failure the viewer has had or can reproduce in ten seconds. Blame two wrong suspects, then name the real mechanism and close on the phrase the title used.
best_for: a tool did something that looks wrong
an 'it says it worked, but' moment the viewer can reproduce
also_for: a design that looks stupid from outside, when the viewer meets it as a failure
avoid_for: architecture and concept topics with no visible symptom
signals: the viewer can reproduce the failure themselves
a tool reports success while something is wrong
there is a literal output, message or screen to show

beats.name: The symptom
beats.job: The exact input and the wrong output, with real values, happening to the viewer.

beats.name: Wrong suspect 2
beats.job: The next thing to blame. It happens there too.

beats.name: Turn
beats.job: One short sentence: nothing is broken, the tool is answering a different question.

beats.name: Mechanism
beats.job: Two or three facts, each with a number or a named part.

beats.name: Root cause
beats.job: One sentence the viewer can repeat.

beats.name: Callback
beats.job: The title's phrase, now explained. A one-line fix may follow, because it is the payoff.

hooks.shape: You [did one small thing]. And [tool] insists you [did something else].
[Tool] can obviously [do X]. Try [a tiny test anyone can run] and you get [the wrong result].
Why does [tool] report [wrong-looking thing] when all you did was [small thing]?

holds: One question (why did it fail?) held until the root cause. Every beat is joined to the next by 'but' or 'so'. The two wrong suspects are the re-openings; the viewer's own objection, spoken aloud, can be a third.
ending: The callback to the title's phrase, or the general rule the case stands for. A one-line fix is allowed.
first_frame: The failure happening: the exact input going in and the wrong output coming out, with the real values readable.
pitfalls: Naming the mechanism in the first sentence
A symptom the viewer cannot picture or reproduce
Three or more mechanisms: one failure, one cause
A callback that opens 'And that's why' or 'So that's how': it reads as a recap. State the title's phrase as a plain sentence
template: You [did one small thing]. And [tool] [reports something that looks wrong]. So you blame [the obvious suspect]. But [the second suspect] does it too. [Tool] is not broken. It [answers a different question]. [Fact with a number]. [Fact]. [Fact]. The real cause: [one sentence]. That is why [the title's phrase]. [One-line fix].
